player.speaker: Revolutionary Delegate
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Emil Barth
line.reaction-briliant.text: The Lehrter delegates were arguing about how many men you could bring. Then your column marched off the train. They'll listen when you tell them what those men can do.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Emil Barth
line.reaction-tactical.text: The Majority Socialists are using your losses to argue for a settlement. I've heard workers repeat it: if this is what the march cost, what will Berlin cost? You need to answer them.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Emil Barth
line.reaction-victory.text: The working districts know your column. Their delegates want to meet you before anyone agrees a settlement with the ministries. I said I'd bring you to them.
line.extra-workers-armed.speaker: Emil Barth
line.extra-workers-armed.text: Word that you armed the workers in Frankfurt reached Berlin yesterday. Our factory battalions are in the streets now; they did not wait to be asked. That is our strength—and exactly what the Majority Socialists point to when they call for order.
line.extra-alternate-history.speaker: Emil Barth
line.extra-alternate-history.text: The ministries tried to stop the rising spreading. Your trains kept bringing delegates and rifles to the next city. We've got columns in Berlin now that they didn't expect to face.
line.callback-frankfurt-held.speaker: Emil Barth
line.callback-frankfurt-held.text: The Rhine-Main delegates have arrived with mandates from Frankfurt. They say the city, station and bridges are still under council guard. I'll have them report to the meeting.
line.callback-frankfurt-lost.speaker: Emil Barth
line.callback-frankfurt-lost.text: You had to leave Frankfurt before its council closed its hand on the whole city. The government still has a functioning administration in the west, and it is using it against us.
line.callback-frankfurt-railways.speaker: Anna Keller
line.callback-frankfurt-railways.text: You told us to take the railway before the proclamations. We did. The government still has telephones, but the delegates arriving at Berlin carry our orders and our account of Frankfurt. Do not waste what we bought you.
line.berlin-awakens.speaker: Emil Barth
line.berlin-awakens.text: Hear the whistles? They've been sounding since dawn. The factory columns are coming out of Moabit, Wedding and the eastern works. Soldiers keep asking if the Kaiser has abdicated. What can we tell them for certain?
line.barth-opening.speaker: Emil Barth
line.barth-opening.text: We can tell them the ministries still hold the centre. Ebert is trying to get inside and form a government. If we want the councils represented there, we have to move.
line.haase-counterargument.speaker: Hugo Haase
line.haase-counterargument.text: Karl, people want the Kaiser gone. That doesn't mean they'll accept a council government. Some of those soldiers want elections and an armistice. If you make them choose between us and Ebert today, we may lose them.
line.liebknecht-question.speaker: Karl Liebknecht
line.liebknecht-question.text: And if Ebert keeps the officers and police in place, who protects our councils while we wait for his elections? Delegate, will your column take the government quarter, or the barracks and stations first?
line.liebknecht-question.choice.governme: Take the Reichstag and government quarter. The councils must be there when power changes hands.
Gain a prestige award and experience for every core formation, but forgo full resupply and the experienced sailor detachment.
line.liebknecht-question.choice.barracks: Secure the barracks, stations and telegraph. I want the loyalist troops cut off before we enter the centre.
Fully resupply every core formation and gain an experienced sailor detachment, but forgo the government-quarter prestige and core-wide experience.
line.haase-government.speaker: Hugo Haase
line.haase-government.text: I won't obstruct the march. Keep contact with the working districts and barracks. If you get into the government quarter and lose the roads behind you, I may not be able to get help through.
line.barth-infrastructure.speaker: Emil Barth
line.barth-infrastructure.text: Then take the stations early. Stop military trains and have the captured barracks elect delegates. I need to know which companies will obey the councils before we turn toward the centre.
line.liebknecht-infrastructure-objection: You'll have the barracks. Ebert may have the ministries by then. I want your column in the centre as soon as the communications are secure. Don't let that become tomorrow's task.
line.ebert-dispatch.speaker: SPD Headquarters
line.ebert-dispatch.text: Political dispatch from SPD headquarters: Friedrich Ebert calls for order, food distribution, an armistice government and elections. He warns that civil war will destroy the republic before it is born. The ministries are preparing to survive the fall of the Kaiser.
line.liebknecht-final.speaker: Karl Liebknecht
line.liebknecht-final.text: Have the column ready to enter the centre. Open the prisons and disarm the troops that resist. When the ministries ask whose orders you carry, send them to the councils. I will go with the delegates.
epilogue.government-quarter-victory.text: Our columns reached the centre before the officials could arrange a new government without us. The Kaiser is gone. Haase has called another meeting; he wants to know which councils can issue orders and expect them to be carried out. Bring your district delegates.
epilogue.government-quarter-defeat.text: The survivors are coming back from the government quarter. We don't hold it, and there are too few men left to try again. I need your officers to tell me who is missing. We can argue about the march after that.
epilogue.military-infrastructure-victory: No loyal troop train got in, and the barracks have elected delegates. Ebert reached the ministries while we secured them. Our guards are outside his doors now. Delegate, will they take their next orders from him or from the councils?
The old command took the stations and armouries back separately. Some comrades got out while our guards held them. I'm trying to assemble those men, but we no longer have enough of Berlin to enforce the councils' orders.
